project.name: AI-Based Healthcare Diagnosis System
project.description: A deep-learning decision-support tool that analyses patient records, lab results and chest X-ray images to suggest likely diagnoses (such as pneumonia, diabetes complications and cardiac conditions) to doctors in hospital outpatient departments. Doctors see a ranked list of probable conditions with confidence scores and use it as a second opinion.
project.data_used: Electronic health records, laboratory values, medical imaging, demographic details (age, sex, ethnicity), prescription history
project.users: Doctors, radiologists and nurses as users; patients as affected people
project.deployment: Integrated into the hospital information system on the hospital's private cloud; used during consultations

risks.title: Unclear clinical scope and intended use
risks.description: The system's intended use (second opinion vs. primary diagnosis) is not clearly defined, so clinicians may over-rely on it for conditions it was never validated for.
risks.mitigation: Write an intended-use statement with excluded conditions; get clinical governance sign-off; show scope limits in the UI.

risks.title: Non-compliance with health data regulations
risks.description: Processing patient records without a documented legal basis or consent may violate health data protection rules such as India's DPDP Act, HIPAA or GDPR.
risks.mitigation: Run a data protection impact assessment; appoint a data protection officer; document legal basis and patient consent.

risks.title: Dataset bias against under-represented patient groups
risks.description: Training data comes mostly from urban hospitals and one ethnic group, so the model may be less accurate for women, rural patients and minority groups.
risks.mitigation: Audit demographic coverage; collect data from multiple sites; apply re-sampling and document dataset limitations in a datasheet.

risks.title: Re-identification of patients from collected records
risks.description: Combining age, postcode and rare diagnoses in collected records could allow individual patients to be identified if the dataset leaks.
risks.mitigation: De-identify at source; apply k-anonymity checks; restrict access with role-based controls and audit logs.

risks.title: Label errors and inconsistent annotations
risks.description: Diagnosis labels taken from discharge summaries and radiology reports contain errors and disagreement between annotating doctors, which corrupts the ground truth.
risks.mitigation: Use double annotation with adjudication; measure inter-annotator agreement; clean noisy labels before training.

risks.title: Sensitive attributes leaking through features
risks.description: Proxy features such as hospital ID or insurance type may encode ethnicity or income and lead to biased predictions even if the attributes are removed.
risks.mitigation: Run proxy-variable analysis; remove or constrain proxy features; test fairness metrics by subgroup.

risks.title: Overfitting and poor generalisation across hospitals
risks.description: The model performs well on the development hospital's data but may fail on images from different scanners or populations.
risks.mitigation: Use cross-site validation and regularisation; report performance with confidence intervals; hold out an external test set.

risks.title: Black-box predictions that doctors cannot explain
risks.description: Deep-learning outputs come without reasons, so doctors cannot check whether the prediction is based on clinically meaningful findings.
risks.mitigation: Add saliency maps and feature-importance explanations; document the model in a model card; train clinicians on how to read the explanations.

risks.title: Incorrect predictions causing missed or wrong diagnosis
risks.description: False negatives may delay treatment of serious disease, while false positives lead to unnecessary tests and patient anxiety.
risks.mitigation: Set sensitivity targets for critical conditions; run prospective clinical validation; require clinician confirmation for every suggestion.

risks.title: Hidden performance gaps across demographic subgroups
risks.description: Average accuracy hides lower accuracy for particular age, sex or ethnic groups, so the system looks safe in testing but harms some patients.
risks.mitigation: Report metrics per subgroup; define acceptable disparity thresholds; involve independent reviewers in the evaluation.

risks.title: Cybersecurity attack on the diagnosis system
risks.description: Adversarial image perturbations, data poisoning or ransomware attacks could alter predictions or take the system offline during care.
risks.mitigation: Penetration testing; encrypted storage and transport; network segmentation; input validation and offline fallback procedures.

risks.title: Automation bias and weak human oversight
risks.description: Busy doctors may accept AI suggestions without checking, so errors pass into the patient record without review.
risks.mitigation: Keep a human-in-the-loop sign-off; display uncertainty clearly; train doctors; log overrides and audit them regularly.

risks.title: Model drift as disease patterns and equipment change
risks.description: New diseases, seasonal changes, updated scanners or changed coding practices cause data drift so accuracy slowly degrades after release.
risks.mitigation: Monitor input distributions and accuracy against confirmed diagnoses; set drift alerts; schedule retraining and revalidation.

risks.title: Unreported incidents and no feedback loop from clinicians
risks.description: Wrong predictions noticed by doctors are not logged or reviewed, so recurring failures are never fixed.
risks.mitigation: Provide a one-click error report; keep an incident register; review incidents monthly with the safety committee.

risks.title: Patient data retained after the system is retired
risks.description: Old models, logs and copies of patient data remain on servers after decommissioning, creating privacy and breach exposure.
risks.mitigation: Define a retention and deletion schedule; securely wipe data and model artefacts; keep a decommissioning certificate.

risks.title: Abrupt withdrawal disrupts clinical workflow
risks.description: Doctors may depend on the tool; retiring it without notice or transition could disrupt care and lose audit history.
risks.mitigation: Plan phased retirement with notice; archive audit logs; provide an alternative workflow.
